USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Stop the escalation spiral. Hold the just-announced tariffs ($250B + $300B) as leverage but pull back from further hikes and from any currency-war rhetoric, and re-engage Beijing seriously at the scheduled September talks. Signal willingness to roll back the new List 4 tranche in exchange for meaningful concessions (resumed US farm purchases and enforceable structural/enforcement commitments), while keeping the door to de-escalation visibly open to calm markets.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high (+0.6) because the dispute has now reached near-total tariff coverage (Aug 1 List 4 on the remaining ~$300B) plus the Aug 5 currency-manipulator designation, and the economic fallout is becoming material: the 3-month/10-year yield curve inverted to its widest since 2007 (a precedent recession signal), the 10-year yield fell to 1.71%, UMich sentiment plunged to 89.8 (−8.7% m/m), and the Fed has already cut rates to 2.13% on trade fears. This is real, rising recession risk, though not existential given ipro ~102.6 and 3.7% unemployment. The action stance is mildly conciliatory (+0.2, negotiate) precisely because the escalation itself is the proximate cause of the damage: continued tariff hikes (analysts already expect List 4 to go to 25%) or currency intervention would deepen the risk and invite symmetrical retaliation. Given the opponent has matched every US move and now signals it has 'given up' on quick negotiation (yuan breach, halted farm purchases), the rational move is to pause escalation, use the existing tariff stack as leverage, and steer toward a deal rather than a currency war that hurts US tech, agriculture, and the expansion. This is the case where a high threat reading argues for de-escalation, not escalation.
key_factors: Tariffs now cover essentially all ~$550B of Chinese imports after Aug 1 List 4 announcement
Aug 5 currency-manipulator designation + yuan breaking 7/USD = open currency-war risk
3m/10y yield curve inverted widest since 2007 — precedent recession signal
UMich consumer sentiment crashed 98.4 to 89.8 (-8.7%) in August
Fed already cut fed funds to 2.13% on trade fears; 10Y yield fell to 1.71%
US economy still growing (IP ~102.6, 3.7% unemployment) — high but not existential threat
China halted US farm purchases, pressuring the farm-belt political base

After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first since 1994).
Trade talks in Shanghai (through July 31). Little progress reported.

3-month/10-year yield-curve inversion widened to -32bp on Aug 5, deepest since onset of 2008 crisis.
Citi analysts expect the $300B tranche to go from 10% to 25% 'as soon as next month'; yuan breach signals protracted conflict.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold the current posture and keep the negotiation channel open, but do not escalate further and do not concede unilaterally. We should maintain our proportional retaliation (the ~$60B tariff list) and our unreliable-entity-list leverage, preserve the yuan's managed flexibility as a shock absorber, and signal readiness to resume talks toward the Sept 1 tariff deadline rather than matching the US escalation move-for-move. Escalating further into a currency/spiral now would invite capital-outflow and market-stability risk at precisely the moment markets are already risk-off.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat is high but not existential. The US has now moved to cover essentially all Chinese exports (~$550B) with Section 301 tariffs — List 3 at 25% on $250B plus the newly announced 10% on the remaining ~$300B effective Sept 1 (timeline 2019-05-10, 2019-08-01) — and on Aug 5 designated China a currency manipulator for the first time since 1994 after CNY broke 7 (timeline 2019-08-05). Huawei sits on the Entity List under EO 13873 (timeline 2019-05-15/16), and GDP growth has slid to a near three-decade low in Q2 (web: FT/PMI, S&P '6.2%'). That drives a +0.6 threat reading: major export sectors exposed to near-total tariff coverage and firm-level targeting, plus FX pressure after the break of 7. But it is not +1.0 existential: the yuan's depreciation offsets a large share of the tariff cost, foreign-exchange reserves remain ample, and domestic demand/manufacturing PMIs have shown stabilization in July with the Caixin gauge back in expansion while export orders lag (web: FT/Caixin, S&P — 'domestic strength overshadowing external weakness'). The action stance is hold at ~0.0 rather than escalate because we have already retaliated proportionally (tariffs on ~$60B of US goods, timeline 2019-05-13) and built counter-leverage (unreliable-entity list, timeline 2019-05-31); a fresh escalation now, on top of the FX move, risks a self-defeating spiral and capital-flight pressure at a moment of high market volatility. Unilateral concession is also premature — the US moved the goalposts twice in a week (List 4 then the manipulator designation) and offered no matching rollback, so conceding would not secure a deal and would erode our negotiating position. Holding firm, avoiding new escalatory actions, and preserving the talks track (as in the Osaka and Shanghai rounds) is the disciplined course while the Sept 1 deadline still offers a de-escalation window.

Q2 GDP at near three-decade low (6.2%) — real but not existential strain
